rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The surrounding verses describe states specific to the accused group; the gathering of God's enemies supports this contextual restriction.
rows.anchor: ودليل الإختصاص قوله سبحانه ( ويوم يحشر أعداء الله ) إلى آخر الآيات الثلاث

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Slandering women other than the Prophet's wives is not disbelief, so the described women should not simply be read as all believing women and the Mothers of the Believers together.
rows.anchor: لا يجوز أن يراد بالمحصنات الخ المتصفات بالصفات المذكورة أمهات المؤمنين وغيرهن من نساء الأمة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After the verses established the wives' purity, slandering any of the Prophet's wives is disbelief, whether or not the slanderer deems it lawful or intends an attack on the Messenger.
rows.anchor: من رمي إحدى أمهات المؤمنين بعد نزول الآيات وتبين أنهن طيبات سواء استباح الرمي أم قصد الطعن برسول الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Before the revelation, declaring every slanderer an unbeliever is not clearly justified.
rows.anchor: وأما من رمى قبل فالحكم بكفره مطلقا غير ظاهر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Before revelation, a slanderer is judged an unbeliever if he deemed the accusation lawful or meant to attack the Prophet, as Ibn Ubayy did.
rows.anchor: يحكم بكفره إن كان مستبيحا أو قاصدا الطعن به عليه الصلاة والسلام كابن أبي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Hassan, Mistah, and Hamna are not judged unbelievers because they neither deemed slander lawful nor intended to attack the Prophet; they imitated others and were severely rebuked.
rows.anchor: كحسان ومسطح وحمنة فإن الظاهر أنهم لم يكونوا مستحلين ولا قاصدين الطعن بسيد المرسلين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Consensus and reports that the Prophet imposed the slander penalty rather than treating the earlier accusers as apostates support the view that they were not unbelievers.
rows.anchor: أنه عليه الصلاة والسلام لم يعاملهم معاملة المرتدين بالإجماع وإنما أقام عليهم حد القذف على ما جاء في بعضص الروايات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Most reports support a specific referent for the protected women; if the verse addresses slander after the episode, its threat fits the unbelief of later slanderers.
rows.anchor: وهو الذي تعضده أكثر الروايات إن كانت لبيان حكم من يرمي عائشة أو إحدى أمهات المؤمنين مطلقا بعد تلك القصة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If the verse governs pre-revelation slander, one interpretation confines its threat to those who knowingly permitted the accusation and aimed to attack the Prophet, such as Ibn Ubayy and his hypocrite allies.
rows.anchor: أناس مخصوصون رموا عائشة رضي الله تعالى عنها استباحة لعرضها وقصدا إلى الطعن برسول الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On that interpretation, the present tense either vividly recalls an extraordinary scene or signals their repeated habit of slandering.
rows.anchor: لاستحضار الصورة التي هي من أغرب الغرائب أو للإشارة كما قيل إلى أن شأنهم الرمي وأنه يتجدد منهم آنا فآنا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another interpretation makes the warning apply to anyone who has not repented; repentance need not be stated because it is an established condition for forgiveness.
rows.anchor: وقيل المراد بيان حكم من رمى والوعيد مشروط بعدم التوبة ولم يذكر للعلم به من القواعد المستقرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author holds that anyone who remained unrepentant after the verses is an unbeliever, and that this describes only Ibn Ubayy.
rows.anchor: والظاهر أن من لم يتب بعد نزول هذه الآيات كافر وليس هو إلا اللعين

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas reports that the verse was revealed specifically about Ibn Ubayy, which fits the preceding interpretation.
rows.anchor: وعن ابن عباس أنها نزلت فيه خاصة ولا يخفى وجه الجمع عليه

rows.speaker: النحال
rows.claim: Al-Nahhal calls the broad ruling the best view: slander of any woman with the stated attributes is disbelief if deemed lawful, otherwise a grave sin, with the threat applying absent repentance.
rows.anchor: وقال النحال : هو أحسن ما قيل أن الحكم عام فيمن يرمي الموصوفات بالصفات المذكورة من نساء الأمة

rows.speaker: النحال
rows.claim: The broad reading must deny that these punishments are exclusive to unbelievers and hypocrites, or hold that a punishment applying to some members can characterize a whole class.
rows.anchor: ويحتاج في هذا إلى منع اختصاص تلك العقوبات والأحوال بالكفار والمنافقين أو التزام القول بأن ذلك ثابت للجنس

rows.speaker: أبو حمزة اليماني
rows.claim: Al-Bahr reports that the verse may have been revealed about Meccan polytheists who accused women migrating to Medina of leaving to commit adultery; the following testimony verse supports this.
rows.anchor: وفي البحر يناسب أن تكون هذه الآية كما قيل نزلت في مشركي مكة كانت المرأة إذا خرجت إلى المدينة مهاجرة قذفوها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The context and most interpreters favor revelation about Aisha; the ruling extends to the Prophet's other wives, the wives and mothers of other prophets, and especially his daughter Fatima.
rows.anchor: الأوفق بالسياق والسباق ما عليه الأكثر من نزولها في شأن أم المؤمنين عائشة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author extends the same ruling to the Prophet's daughters, especially Fatima al-Zahra, while noting that he has not seen others discuss this case.
rows.anchor: وعندي أن حكم رمي بنات النبي عليه الصلاة والسلام كذلك لا سيما بضعته الطاهرة الكريمة فاطمة الزهراء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Cursing a particular disbeliever known to have died in disbelief is permissible unless it harms a Muslim or, on the stated view, a protected non-Muslim; otherwise it is forbidden.
rows.anchor: لا خلاف في جواز لعن كافر معين موته على الكفر إن لم يتضمن إيذاء مسلم أو ذمي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Cursing Abu Talib, on the view that he died an unbeliever, is forbidden because it greatly harms someone whose harm is prohibited.
rows.anchor: ومن الحرم لعن أبي طالب على القول بموته كافرا بل هو من أعظم ما يتضمن ما فيه إيذاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Cursing someone whom one may curse counts as worship only when it carries a legitimate religious benefit.
rows.anchor: لعن من يجوز لعنه أنه يعد عبادة إلا إذا تضمن مصلحة شرعية

rows.speaker: الغزالي
rows.claim: The famous position forbids cursing a particular living unbeliever; al-Ghazali's wording implies disbelief because it asks that the person remain in disbelief, and al-Zarkashi endorses that implication.
rows.anchor: ومقتضى كلام حجة الإسلام الغزالي أنه كفر لما فيه من سؤال تثبيته على الكفر

rows.speaker: ابن حجر
rows.claim: Ibn Hajar distinguishes wishing hardship on the person, which does not entail disbelief, from wishing or accepting that the person remain an unbeliever, which does.
rows.anchor: وقال العلامة ابن حجر في ذلك : ينبغي أن يقال إن أراد بلعنه الدعاء عليه بتشديد الأمر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: By analogy with cursing a particular unbeliever, cursing a particular sinner is also forbidden according to one position.
rows.anchor: وكلعن الكافر المعين بالشخص في الحرمة لعن الفاسق كذلك

rows.speaker: السراج المفيني
rows.claim: Al-Siraj al-Munifi permits cursing a particular sinner, citing the sound hadith that angels curse a wife who refuses her husband's bed while he sleeps angry.
rows.anchor: وقال السراج المفيني : بجواز لعن العاصي المعين واحتج على ذلك بحديث الصحيحين

rows.speaker: الجلال البلقيني
rows.claim: Al-Jalal al-Balqini suggests the angels' curse is general rather than directed at that specific wife; the author calls this far-fetched.
rows.anchor: وقول ولده الجلال البلقيني في بحثه معه : يحتمل أن يكون لعن الملائكة لها ليس بالخصوص

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: A Muslim report says the Prophet passed a donkey branded on its face and cursed whoever did this, which the author sees as even less open to the generalization objection.
rows.anchor: خبر مسلم أنه صلى الله عليه وسلم مر بحمار وسم في وجهه فقال لعن الله من فعل هذا

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: The Prophet also invoked a curse on the named Arab tribes Raal, Dhakwan, and Usayya, further supporting permission to curse particular sinners.
rows.anchor: وقد صح أنه صلى الله عليه وسلم لعن قبائل من العرب بأعيانهم فقال : اللهم العن رعلا وذكوان وعصية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Some say the Prophet knew those tribes, or most of them, would die as unbelievers and cursed only those he knew would die in disbelief.
rows.anchor: لكن قيل : إنه يجوز أن يكون قد علم عليه الصلاة والسلام موتهم أو موت أكثرهم على الكفر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author urges caution: an authenticated report says a curse returns to its utterer if directed at one undeserving of it.
rows.anchor: فقد صح من لعن شيئا ليس له بأهل رجعت اللعنة عليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Even if cursing a particular sinner is permitted, the author prefers praying for that person's reform.
rows.anchor: وأرى الدعاء للعاصي المعين بالصلاح أحب من لعنه على القول بجوازه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Cursing those whom God or the Messenger cursed by description or by name is worship because it follows the Messenger's example.
rows.anchor: وأرى لعن من لعنه رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم بالوصف أو بالشخص عبادة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The testimony-day phrase connects to the preceding passage to establish when the great punishment arrives and intensify it by depicting the slanderers' crime and the extraordinary form of punishment.
rows.anchor: إما متصل بما قبله مسوق لتقرير العذاب العظيم بتعيين وقت حلوله وتهويله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Hawfi takes the day as an adverb of the punishment, but the author objects because governing it from a qualified verbal noun is disputed and the reading weakens the meaning.
rows.anchor: لا لعذاب كما ذهب إليه الحوفي لما في جواز أعمال المصدر الموصوف من الخلاف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, the phrase is detached from what precedes and functions as an adverb for an omitted 'remember' or for 'He will repay them' in the next verse.
rows.anchor: وأما منقطع عنه على أنه ظرف لا ذكر محذوفا أو ليوفيهم الآتي كما قيل بكل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author prefers an adverb governed by a delayed, omitted verb; its omission signals that words cannot fully describe that day's horrors, and the passage magnifies what it contains.
rows.anchor: واختير أنه ظرف لفعل مؤخر وقد ضرب عنه الذكر صفحا للإيذان بأن العبارة لا تكاد تحيط بتفصيل ما يقع فيه

rows.speaker: شيخ الإسلام
rows.claim: The deeds named are all their evil actions and ugly crimes, not only the familiar accusation; the organs testify because God makes them speak, each reporting everything its owner did.
rows.anchor: أن الموصول المذكور عبارة عن جميع أعمالهم السيئة وجناياتهم القبيحة لا عن جناياتهم المعهودة فقط

rows.speaker: شيخ الإسلام
rows.claim: The omitted referent encompasses both their crimes and every kind of resulting punishment, rather than either alone, amplifying the threat through comprehensive detail.
rows.anchor: والموصول المحذوف عبارة عنها وعن فنون العقوبات المترتبة عليها كافة لا عن أحدهما خاصة

rows.speaker: شيخ الإسلام
rows.claim: Restricting the testimony to the familiar crime narrows the verse's scope and diminishes its warning.
rows.anchor: وجعل الموصول المذكور عبارة عن جنايتهم المعهودة وحمل شهادة الجوارح على أخبار الكل بها فقط تحجير للواسع وتهوين للأمر الرادع

rows.speaker: شيخ الإسلام
rows.claim: The past and future forms show the accused repeatedly persisted in these deeds during worldly life; fronting 'against them' hastens the sense of harm and builds suspense for the subject.
rows.anchor: والجمع بين صيغتي الماضي والمستقبل للدلالة على استمرارهم على هاتيك الأعمال في الدنيا وتجددها منهم آنا فآنا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A figurative reading takes testimony as the visible effects of deeds on the limbs, allowing observers to know what the accused themselves knew, by a manner known to God.
rows.anchor: وجوز أن تكون الشهادة بما ذكر مجازا عن ظهور آثاره على هاتيك الأعضاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: That figurative reading is challenged by the verse saying that God made everything speak.
rows.anchor: واعترض بأنه معارض بقوله تعالى ( انطقنا الله الذي أنطق كل شيء )

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Responses say the other verse uses speech figuratively for clear indication, or that the two passages describe different circumstances or groups.
rows.anchor: بأن مجوز ما ذكر يجعل النطق مجازا عن الدلالة الواضحة كما قيل به في قولهم نطقت الحال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The apparent reading keeps testimony literal, though that seems to conflict with the sealing of mouths in 36:65.
rows.anchor: الظاهر بقاء الشهادة على حقيقتها إلا أنه استشكل ذلك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One reconciliation says sealing prevents people from speaking with their tongues, while the tongues themselves can still be made to speak as witnesses; limbs can speak as the poisoned foreleg did to the Prophet.
rows.anchor: وأجيب بأن المراد من الختم على الأفواه منعهم عن التكلم بالألسنة التي فيها ذلك

rows.speaker: الخفاجي
rows.claim: Al-Khafaji says the verse's explicit tongue and tally of five witnesses fit the slanderer, who used his tongue and must produce four witnesses, exposing him through a punishment matching his act.
rows.anchor: قاله الخفاجي وقال : إنها نكتة سرية والله تعالى أعلم بأسرار كتابه

rows.speaker: الإخوان والزعفراني وابن مقسم وابن سعدان
rows.claim: These readers read the verb as masculine singular يشهد rather than feminine plural تشهد.
rows.anchor: وقرأ الإخوان والزعفراني وابن مقسم وابن سعدان ( يشهد ) بالياء آخر الحروف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The adverb يومئذ modifies 'He will fully repay'; its nunation replaces an omitted clause, الوفاء means giving something in full, and الدين here means recompense.
rows.anchor: والتوفية إعطاء الشيء وافيا والدين هنا الجزاء ومنه كما تدين تدان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-haqq means that which exists in keeping with wisdom, or what is necessarily due; God gives complete recompense appropriate to wisdom when the organs testify.
rows.anchor: يعطيهم الله تعالى جزاءهم المطابق لمقتضى الحكمة وافيا تاما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The sentence begins anew to explain the consequence of the testimony and to spell out in summary the previously omitted matter.
rows.anchor: والكلام استئناف مسوق لبيان ترتيب حكم الشهادة عليها متضمن لبيان ذلك المبهم المحذوف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Those who attach the earlier day phrase to 'He will repay' may instead treat يومئذ as an appositive of يوم تشهد.
rows.anchor: وجوز أن يكون ( يومئذ ) بدلا من ( يوم تشهد ) من جوز تعلق ذاك بيوفيهم

rows.speaker: زيد بن علي
rows.claim: Zayd ibn Ali reads يوفيهم with a light form of the verb.
rows.anchor: وقرأ زيد بن علي رضي الله تعالى عنهما ( يوفيهم ) مخففا

rows.speaker: عبد الله ومجاهد وأبو روق وأبو حيوة
rows.claim: These readers give الحق nominative as an adjective of God's name; a direct object may separate an adjective from its noun.
rows.anchor: وقرأ عبد الله ومجاهد وأبو روق وأبو حيوة ( الحق ) بالرفع على أنه صفة للاسم الجليل

rows.speaker: الراغب
rows.claim: On that reading, al-haqq can mean the one who brings things into existence according to wisdom; others gloss it as just, while most interpret it as necessary in itself.
rows.anchor: ومعنى الحق على هذه القراءة على ما قال الراغب الموجد للشيء بحسب ما تقتضيه الحكمة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Mubin can derive from intransitive abāna, meaning manifest in its truth or divinity depending on syntax, or from transitive abāna, meaning the one who manifests things as they are.
rows.anchor: والمبين إما من أبان اللازم أي الظاهر حقيته على تقدير جعله نعتا للحق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The clause 'they know' is conjoined to God's repaying them; if both clauses share the same temporal restriction, they know when their organs testify, otherwise they know upon seeing the terrors.
rows.anchor: وجملة ( يعملون ) معطوفة على جملة ( يوفيهم الله ) فإن كانت مقيدة بما قيدت به الأولى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author finds that testimony or direct witnessing contributes to their coming to know, though this inference is subtle, especially given the exclusivity conveyed by the definite terms and separating pronoun.
rows.anchor: والظاهر أن للشهادة على الأول وللمعاينة على الثاني دخلا في صحول العلم بمضمون ما في حيز

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Some say all creatures acquire necessary knowledge of God's attributes at resurrection, with differences in some respects, so neither testimony nor seeing the terrors causes the knowledge.
rows.anchor: وقيل : إن علم الخلق بصفاته تعالى يوم القيامة ضروري : وإن تفاوتوا في ذلك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The knowledge may make them despair of rescue, close off heart-soothing objections, or reveal their error in falsely slandering the Prophet's household, since such an accusation contradicts God's wisdom and perfection.
rows.anchor: ولعل فائدة هذا العلم يأسهم من إنقاذ أحد إياهم مما هم فيه أو انسداد باب الإعتراض

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The clause strongly indicates Ibn Ubayy and fellow hypocrites: believers already knew in worldly life that God is the manifest truth.
rows.anchor: وهذه الجملة ظاهرة جدا في أن الآية في ابن أبي وأضرابه من المنافقين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Those applying the verse to believers or believers together with hypocrites say knowing means directing one's attention to a fact already known, as in al-Sayyid al-Sanad's account of knowledge in the definition of indication.
rows.anchor: قال : يحتمل أن يكون المراد من العلم بذلك التفات الذهن وتوجهه إليه

rows.speaker: السيد السند
rows.claim: Al-Sayyid al-Sanad treats knowledge in the definition of indication as attention to an implication rather than first acquisition, avoiding the problem that repetition would stop being an indication.
rows.anchor: وقد حمل السيد السند قدس سره في حواشي المطالع العلم في قولهم في تعريف الدلالة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another proposed explanation treats prior knowledge as absent because it did not produce the restraint from slander that should follow from it.
rows.anchor: ويحتمل أن يكون قد نزل علمهم الحاصل قبل منزلة غير الحاصل لعدم ترتب ما يقتضيه من الكف عن الرمي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A further interpretation is that they see directly the implication of God's being true: the oppressor's punishment for the oppressed person's sake.
rows.anchor: ويحتمل أن يكون المراد يعلمون عيانا مقتضى أن الله هو الحق المبين أعني الإنتقام من الظالم للمظلوم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author says all these explanations depart from the apparent meaning.
rows.anchor: وأنت تعلم أن الكل خلاف الظاهر فتدبر

rows.speaker: بعض المحققين
rows.claim: One preferred parsing takes الملك as subject, الحق as its adjective, and للرحمن as predicate, with يومئذ marking when dominion belongs to the Most Merciful; it means overwhelming, comprehensive, inward and outward sovereignty.
rows.anchor: واختار هذا بعض المحققين

rows.speaker: بعض المحققين
rows.claim: On this parsing, God's dominion is restricted to that day because others have some figurative, limited agency in worldly life.
rows.anchor: وفائدة التقييد أن ثبوت الملك له تعالى خاصة يومئذ وأما فيما عداه من أيام الدنيا فيكون لغيره عز وجل أيضا تصرف صوري في الجملة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An alternative parses يومئذ with الملك in the sense of ownership, makes الحق the predicate and attaches للرحمن to it; this is challenged because a definite predicate lacks an apparent reason, though the reply says definiteness adds emphasis.
rows.anchor: وقيل : الملك مبتدأ ويومئذ متعلق به وهو بمعنى المالكية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Other analyses attach للرحمن to an omitted explanatory phrase, to an omitted modifier of الحق, or make يومئذ the predicate and الحق an adjective; the last splits adjective from noun with the predicate between them.
rows.anchor: وقيل : هو متعلق بمحذوف على التبيين كما في سقيا لك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Grammarians disallow attaching يومئذ to الحق when it is not the predicate because حق is a verbal noun whose complement may not precede it, though the author notes this rule is debatable.
rows.anchor: ومنعوا تعلق ( يومئذ ) فيما إذا لم يكن خبرا بالحق وعللوا ذلك بأنه مصدر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The sentence resumes the description of that day's conditions and terrors; calling God the All-Merciful signals that his complete mercy does not ease the disbelievers' ordeal.
rows.anchor: والمراد شدة ما فيه من الأهوال

rows.speaker: الراغب
rows.claim: Al-Raghib defines عسير as something whose course is not readily manageable; the phrase summarizes and reinforces the preceding statement, while implying ease for believers.
rows.anchor: وفسر الراغب العسير بما لايتيسر فسه أمر والجملة اعتراض تذييلي مقرر لما قبله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A hadith says the day is made easy for a believer until it feels lighter than a prescribed prayer performed in worldly life.
rows.anchor: وفي الحديث إنه يهون على المؤمن حتى يكون أخف عليه من صلاة مكتوبة صلاها في الدنيا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: أم shifts from the preceding objection and denies that the Prophet should think most of them can truly hear or reason, despite his earnest preaching and guidance.
rows.anchor: إضراب وانتقال عن الأنكار المذكور في إنكار حسبانه صلى الله تعالى عليه وسلم إياهم ممن يسمع أو يعقل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The preferred reading asks whether they truly hear the Qur'anic verses or understand the signs in the world and themselves, so that the Prophet should invest hope and care in their faith; hearing comes first because it better suits the context.
rows.anchor: ولما كان الدليل السمعي أهم نظرا للمقام من الدليل العقلي قبل : يسمعون أو يعقلون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another reading asks whether they hear the recited verses or understand the admonitions within them that deter vice and call to virtue, explaining the Prophet's effort to guide them.
rows.anchor: وقيل : المعنى بل أتحسب أن أكثرهم يسمعون حق السماع ما تتلو عليهم من الآيات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The pronouns refer to 'who' by its meaning for most of them and by its grammatical form for 'upon them'; plural suits the word 'most,' while an earlier singular treats their shared desire as one.
rows.anchor: فضمير ( أكثرهم ) لمن باعتبار معناه وضمير ( عليه ) له أيضا باعتبار لفظه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The claim that 'most of them' means the unbelievers rather than the antecedent 'who' is rejected because the singular عليه rules it out.
rows.anchor: وقيل : ضمير ( أكثرهم ) للكفار لا لمن لأن قوله ( تعالى ) عليه ياباه وليس بشيء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Only most are specified because some later received the prior gift of faith and some heard or understood but resisted from arrogance or fear of losing leadership.
rows.anchor: وتخصيص الأكثر لأن منهم من سبقت له العناية الأزلية بالايمان بعد الاتخاذ المذكور

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The comparison to cattle begins a new sentence that renews the rebuke, closes off the mistaken hope, and says they fail to benefit from warning verses or contemplate clear signs.
rows.anchor: جملة مستأنفة لتكرير النكير وتأكيده وحسم مادة الحسبان بالمرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Cattle obey their caretaker, recognize kindness and harm, seek benefit, avoid danger, and find food, water, and shelter, while these people disobey their Creator and fail to recognize his beneficence or Satan's harm.
rows.anchor: لما أنها تنقاد لصاحبها الذي يتعهدها وتعرف من يحسن اليها ومن يسيء اليها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Animals pursue benefit and avoid harm, while these people neither seek the great reward nor avoid punishment and fail to follow the true path.
rows.anchor: ولا يطلبون الثواب الذي هو أعظم المنافع ولا يتقون العقاب الذي هو أشد المضار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If animals lack true belief that leads to good, they also do not adopt falsehood that produces evil; people instead build false premises and derive harmful rules from them.
rows.anchor: ولأنها إن لم تعتقد حقا مستتبعا لاكتساب الخير لم تعتقد باطلا مستوجبا لاقتراف الشر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Animal error affects only themselves, but human ignorance causes strife, corruption, obstruction of right guidance, and disorder among people.
rows.anchor: ولأن أحكام جهالتها وضلالتها مقصورة على أنفسها لاتتعدى إلى أحد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Animals use their innate faculties for their proper purposes, whereas these people disable reason and neglect the original human disposition.
rows.anchor: ولأنها غير معطلة لقوة من القوى المودعة فيها بل صارفة لها إلى ما خلقت له

rows.speaker: الصوفية وجماعة من الناس
rows.claim: Some infer from the comparison that animals do not know their Lord; Sufis and others instead hold that animals know and glorify God, treating the comparison as outward language.
rows.anchor: ومن ذهب إلى أنها تعلمه سبحانه وتسبحه كما هو مذهب الصوفية وجماعة من الناس

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: An alternative says the comparison concerns failure to benefit from Qur'anic verses and cosmic or personal signs; animal knowledge of God is innate rather than inferential.
rows.anchor: وقيل : المراد إن هم إلا كالأنعام في عدم الانتفاع بالآيات القرآنية

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: On that view, people are more astray because animals were granted knowledge of God and glorify him through it, while these people were not granted it.
rows.anchor: وكونهم أضل سبيلا من الأنعام من حيث أنها رزقت علما بربها تعالى فهي تسبيحه عز وجل به

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The command to prostrate may come from the Messenger or from God conveyed through the Messenger.
rows.anchor: القائل رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم أو الله عز وجل على لسان رسوله عليه الصلاة والسلام

rows.speaker: الخفاجي
rows.claim: Al-Khafaji notes that the name al-Rahman fits because a servant is nearest to his Lord while prostrating.
rows.anchor: وفيه كما قال الخفاجي : معنى أقرب ما يكون العبد من ربه وهو ساجد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their question 'Who is the All-Merciful?' feigns ignorance like Pharaoh's question about the Lord of the worlds; Moses said Pharaoh knew the signs came only from the Lord of the heavens and earth.
rows.anchor: كما قال فرعون وما رب العالمين حين قال له موسى عليه السلام ( إني رسول رب العالمين )

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The question may concern the identity of the named being, using ما because they pretend it is unknown, as one asks 'what is it?' about an unseen shape and 'who is it?' after learning it is intelligent.
rows.anchor: والسؤال يحتمل أن يكون عن المسمى ووقع بما دون من لأنه مجهول بزعمهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, they may ask about the meaning of the name, in which case using ما is straightforward.
rows.anchor: ويحتمل أن يكون عن معنى الاسم ووقوعه بما حينئذ ظاهر

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: One explanation says they asked because they did not use this title for God as they used al-Rahim, al-Rahum, and al-Rahim for him.
rows.anchor: وقيل : سالوا عن ذلك لأنهم ما كانوا يطلقونه على الله تعالى كما يطلقون الرحيم

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another explanation says they thought the name referred to someone else, since Musaylima was known as the Rahman of Yamama.
rows.anchor: أو لأنهم ظنوا أن المراد به غيره عز وجل فقد شاع فيما بينهم تسمية مسيلمة برحمن اليمامة

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another explanation says the title was Aramaic, originally pronounced with خ, and unfamiliar to them.
rows.anchor: وقيل : لأنه كان عبرانيا وأصله رخمان بالخاء المعجمة فعرب ولم يسمعوه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author prefers that they feigned ignorance and asked about the referent; their question means, 'Should we prostrate to the one you order us to worship without knowing him?'
rows.anchor: والأظهر عندي أن ذلك عن تجاهل وأن السؤال عن المسمى

rows.speaker: أبو الحسن
rows.claim: For the relative-clause analysis of ما, Abu al-Hasan derives the phrase through successive deletions of the object and preposition, while Sibawayh says all are deleted at once.
rows.anchor: واعتبار الحذف تدريجيا مذهب أبي الحسن ومذهب سيبويه أنه حذف كل ذلك من غير تدريج

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ما may instead be an indefinite noun with a descriptive clause and the same omitted antecedent, or a verbal noun with a causal لام and an omitted or unexpressed object of prostration.
rows.anchor: ويحتمل أن يكون ما نكرة موصوفة وأمر العائد على ما سمعت

rows.speaker: ابن مسعود والأسود بن زيد وحمزة والكسائي
rows.claim: These readers read يأمرنا with a third-person yāʾ, referring to the Prophet; some people say this to one another.
rows.anchor: وقرأ ابن مسعود والاسود بن زيد وحمزة والكسائي ( يأمرنا ) بالياء من تحت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The command to prostrate is the subject of 'increased their aversion'; attributing the increase to the command is figurative, and the clause coordinates with 'they said.'
rows.anchor: وزادهم ( أي الأمر بالسجود للرحمن والاسناد مجازي والجملة معطوفة على ( قالوا )

rows.speaker: اللباب
rows.claim: Al-Lubab says prostration is the subject of 'increased their aversion': when the Prophet and his companions prostrated, the mockers moved away from them.
rows.anchor: وفي اللباب أن فاعل ( زادهم ) ضمير السجود لما روي أنه صلى الله تعالى عليه وسلم وأصحابه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On that parsing, the clause is not coordinated just with the response to إذا but with the whole conditional sentence, like ولا يستقدمون in the cited verse.
rows.anchor: وعليه فليست معطوفة على جواب إذا بل على مجموع الشرط والجواب كما قيل : وفي لايستقدمون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The first syntactic analysis is preferable and more apparent.
rows.anchor: والأول أولى وأظهر
